newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen end Tokyo 1996 with small gains.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen end Tokyo 1996 with small gains.

text.p: The key September three-month Euroyen futures contract ended on Monday with small gains from end-year position adjustments.
Trade was sluggish with most of the local institutional investors out of the market, traders said.

"Despite the weak yen, the contract's bottom was well underpinned by dealers' position adjustments," said a bank dealer. The September ended at 99.25 after recovering from the day's low of 99.22. Friday's settlement was 99.24.
Japan's money markets close for New Year holidays on Monday and reopen on January 6.
Cash money market rates were mixed.

The key overnight call rate fell to around 0.42-0.45 percent in response to massive fund availability there, traders said. Friday's weighted average rate was 0.48. The Bank of Japan's operation this morning was a neutral one, which was in line with expectations.

In the long-end of the market, benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CD) were issued at 0.53 percent, the highest rate since October 3. The rate rise from the previous 0.52 percent reflected small, but strong demand for funds over holidays, traders said. The volume was only 10 billion yen.
